digest.component_or_area: rebar repository — comprehensive code, architecture, documentation, and test quality evaluation
propositions: 87 source modules exceed the documented 500-LOC target, with 206 functions above complexity 15, concentrating orchestration logic in high-risk hotspots (compute(), import_tickets()) that should be decomposed at call-graph seams while maintaining the existing shrink-only ratchet

Broad mypy passing conceals 687 errors under --disallow-untyped-defs; only rebar.graph and rebar.grounding enforce strictness, requiring package-by-package expansion and narrowed ignore_missing_imports at transport boundaries

Architectural enforcement is selective (high-risk seams have checks, low-risk paths lack repository-wide DAG contract), exposing new cross-layer imports to review-only governance rather than systemic gates

Documentation/configuration examples contradict runtime behavior (--assignee alice vs email-required, removed .rebar/config.conf vs rebar.toml, stale optional-dependency and mypy advisory descriptions) and drift checks are not gating

Python 3.11 xdist worker dies spuriously in test_opcert_service_app.py::test_matching_guard_is_accepted after ~11.4k passed tests with 'node down: Not properly terminated,' observed in 4 Verified runs and 2 scheduled mirror runs, requiring teardown/serialization investigation to restore gate reliability

Two reproducible test-environment assumptions fail (UTF-8 decode of editor_assets binaries in help_overview_coverage.py, shallow Git checkout missing historical objects in attestation_signing.py) despite strong behavioral oracles and must be fixed with explicit enumeration and self-contained fixtures
